title: Today on X
windowLabel: 7:00 a.m. Tuesday, Nov. 17 to 7:03 a.m. Wednesday, Nov. 18, B.C. time
method: Built from the News & Events brief’s X summary, then checked against the original posts via X. Counts are from that check and may have changed. The home timeline covered 1,874 posts from 223 accounts (replies excluded). NHL trade items in the brief came from a separate public search, not from accounts we follow, and are omitted here. Andy Lee’s reposts are shown as the original posts by Ezra Levant and Bob Mackin.
trendsNote: X’s worldwide list often reflects the most active regions at this hour, which is why it may look different from the Canada and U.S. lists.

themes.title: More outages, and cyber-attack claims officials say have no evidence behind them
themes.summary: Accounts on the feed linked Tuesday's Apple outage to the week's Microsoft, FAA and Chase problems. @nicksortor said the outages show why voting machines must never be online; @libsoftiktok reported outages "at Apple and Google"; @bennyjohnson tied the wave to a Bill Gates remark and, separately, said CNN and Fox News were "hit with Cyberattack." The Apple outage was real, and CBS News reported the NSA's classified network also went offline Tuesday. Apple said its problem was not a cyberattack, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is "zero evidence" the incidents are connected to hackers or another nation. We found no report of a Google outage. Johnson's CNN/Fox post refers to a real but separate incident: malicious code planted in the Optimizely web tool ran on the sites of 178 organizations; the sites did not crash.
themes.whyItMatters: Real disruptions are being wrapped in an attack story that no official or company has backed.

flags.label: Confirmed
flags.note: Apple's outage and the NSA network outage were reported by CBS News.

flags.label: Disputed
flags.note: No evidence of a cyberattack or a link between the outages; Rubio and Sen. Mark Warner both said so.

source.title: CBS News: Rubio says there's "zero evidence" outages are related

flags.label: Partly true
flags.note: The Optimizely code hack was real, but it was unrelated to the outages and did not crash the sites.

flags.label: Unverified
flags.note: We found no report of a Google outage, and no outlet ties the outages to Bill Gates.

themes.title: Xi greets Trump in person on the tarmac in Shenzhen
themes.summary: @nicksortor posted that Xi Jinping "PERSONALLY" greeted Trump as he left Air Force One, adding his own view that Biden or Harris could not have "commanded this sort of respect." The greeting happened: NBC News and the BBC report Xi met Trump on the tarmac, which NBC says is believed to be a first for any foreign leader arriving in China. Xi was returning the gesture Trump made in Washington in September. The comparison to Biden and Harris is the poster's opinion.
themes.whyItMatters: The welcome sets the tone for Thursday's first three-way Trump–Xi–Putin meeting.

flags.label: Confirmed
flags.note: Reported by NBC News, the BBC and China's foreign ministry.

source.title: NBC News: Xi greets Trump as he arrives in China

themes.title: U.S. strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
themes.summary: @DailyLoud posted that the U.S. "launched NEW AIRSTRIKES against Iran, targeting a missile launch site on Qeshm Island" in retaliation for attacks on U.S. personnel. A U.S. military official confirmed precision strikes on a Revolutionary Guard missile site there, calling them "self-defense" after Iranian attacks including on a U.S. radar site in Bahrain. Iranian officials say the strike did no damage to residential or infrastructure areas.
themes.whyItMatters: The strike was followed Wednesday by Iranian fire at Bahrain and Kuwait, a widening of the exchange.

flags.label: Confirmed
flags.note: Confirmed by a U.S. military official, as reported by CBS News and USA Today.

themes.title: Peltola wins Alaska, settling the Senate
themes.summary: @DecisionDeskHQ projected Tuesday night that Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska's Senate race. NBC News and Fox News also called it: Peltola beat Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan with just over 50% of first-choice votes, so no ranked-choice count was needed. Democrats will hold 56 seats in January.
themes.whyItMatters: It was the last undecided Senate race of the midterms.

themes.title: "Gas suddenly dropped right after the midterms"
themes.summary: @libsoftiktok said it was "very interesting that the price of gas suddenly dropped right after the midterms." Prices have dropped, but not suddenly after the Nov. 3 vote. AAA's national average was $3.78 on Nov. 17, down about 20 cents in a week and about 52 cents in a month, so the decline began before the election. Bloomberg says prices are at their lowest since March as oil supply recovers.
themes.whyItMatters: The price drop is real; the timing the post implies is not.

flags.label: Partly true
flags.note: Prices are falling, but the decline started before the midterms.

source.title: AAA: Gas and diesel prices fall in all 50 states

themes.title: A "fire" at CIA headquarters that firefighters say was smoke from an HVAC unit
themes.summary: @bennyjohnson posted that "a fire has broken out at the CIA Headquarters in Langley," reportedly electrical. @GenFlynn joked about "burn bags." Fairfax County firefighters responded to reports of smoke, found it came from an HVAC unit, reported no injuries and gave the all-clear, according to FOX 5 DC and Patch.
themes.whyItMatters: An equipment problem was framed as a fire at a spy agency, inviting cover-up theories.

flags.label: Disputed
flags.note: Firefighters found smoke from an HVAC unit, not a fire; no one was hurt.

source.title: FOX 5 DC: Smoke from HVAC at CIA headquarters prompts emergency response

themes.title: Musk's 🤦‍♂️ at Transportation Secretary Duffy over Starlink
themes.summary: @elonmusk replied with a face-palm emoji to a clip of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy explaining why the FAA wants a ground-based network. @nicksortor said Starlink "would've saved BILLIONS UPON BILLIONS." Benzinga reported Duffy said the FAA wants a ground-based system because "our airspace is very big," that an earlier Starlink version had technical issues in FAA testing, and that the FAA uses Starlink for some assets in Alaska. The savings figure is the poster's opinion, not a reported finding.
themes.whyItMatters: This follows Monday's claim that the FAA turned down free Starlink terminals.

themes.title: Andy Lee on Carney's China trip: bank branches, a consulate threat and B.C. FOI delays
themes.summary: @RealAndyLeeShow said Canadian media overlooked parts of the China deals, quoting a post on Chinese bank branches; she also reposted @ezralevant saying Carney is making room for more Chinese banks. China's Commerce Ministry, via Xinhua, says the two countries reached "positive consensus" on opening branches of Chinese-funded banks in Canada; Canada's readout of the Carney–Xi meeting does not mention it, and we found no Ottawa comment. She also said only Rebel News defended pro-democracy Chinese-Canadians after a man was filmed threatening a Falun Gong protester outside China's Toronto consulate; the Falun Dafa Association says an arrest warrant was issued and the man has returned to China, which we could not confirm with police. She reposted journalist @bobmackin's report that B.C.'s privacy commissioner let public bodies delay FOI responses for a year. Her post saying Carney once called China Canada's greatest security threat is accurate: he said so at the April 2025 leaders' debate.
themes.whyItMatters: Some of her points are backed by official records; others rest on a single source.

flags.label: Partly true
flags.note: Xinhua reports the bank-branch consensus; Canada's own documents do not mention it.

flags.label: Unverified
flags.note: The Toronto arrest warrant is reported by the Falun Dafa Association, not confirmed by police.

source.title: CTV News: Video captures confrontation outside Chinese consulate

flags.label: Unverified
flags.note: The FOI delay is reported by Bob Mackin's theBreaker; not yet independently confirmed.

flags.label: Confirmed
flags.note: Carney called China Canada's biggest security threat at the April 17, 2025 debate.
